newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to unveil $2.4 billion in diabetes spending.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to unveil $2.4 billion in diabetes spending.

text.p: President Clinton on Friday plans to unveil $2.4 billion in government spending over the next five years to treat diabetes and search for a cure, White House officials said.

The officials, who asked not to be identified, said the money was all included in the balanced-budget legislation that Clinton signed on Tuesday that aims to eliminate the federal budget deficit by the year 2002.
They said Clinton, in an 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) speech at Washington's Georgetown University Medical Centre, planned to highlight the following items:

-- $2.1 billion in Medicare spending over five years to expand an existing programme to help train people covered by the health care programme for the elderly to manage their own treatment for the disease.
-- $150 million earmarked to fund research to find a cure for juvenile diabetes.
-- $150 million to prevent, treat and research a cure for diabetes among Native Americans, who are three times more likely than the national average to suffer from the disease.
